{"id":"01a0fce4-49e5-7822-b5be-82be27e6181e","type":"hazard","summary":"Database connections in deployed environments","content":"In production and staging the app never connects to Postgres directly; every connection goes through a pooler on port 6432 that the platform team manages. Locally, docker-compose exposes Postgres itself on 5432 with no pooler, so the problems below only show up after deploy. The pool is sized at 20 server connections per service, and long transactions starve checkout, so keep transactions short and never hold one open across an HTTP call to the ledger. The pooler runs in transaction mode: session state does not survive between transactions (no SET session variables, no advisory locks across transactions, no LISTEN/NOTIFY), and server-side prepared statements fail with 'prepared statement does not exist'. With psycopg 3 you must connect with `prepare_threshold=None` to turn automatic prepared statements off.","physical":["src/","docker-compose.yml"],"logical":["database"],"tags":["database","postgres"],"criticality":0.7,"confidence":0.8,"status":"active","visibility":"shared","provenance":"human","epistemic":"fact"}

import os

import pytest


@pytest.mark.postgres
def test_invoices_table_exists():
    psycopg = pytest.importorskip("psycopg")
